metadata.title: FIELD//ZERO Earth Western Desert terrain similarity to Moon (Taurus-Littrow) reference terrain, 120 m

model.name: FIELD//ZERO terrain analog similarity model
model.label: TERRAIN ANALOG MODEL: compares four DEM-derived surface-shape metrics only. It is not proof of complete environmental equivalence.
model.disclaimer: Scores describe statistical closeness of terrain-shape metrics to the reference distribution of one Mars site (Jezero) or one Moon site (Taurus-Littrow). They do not describe geology, composition, regolith, gravity, atmosphere, temperature, pressure, radiation, illumination or any other environmental property. No location in this output is a confirmed planetary analog; ranked locations are candidates for further study.

metadata.coordinate_note: Point = WGS84 lon/lat degrees of the Earth cell centre. Feature order equals the row order of the 120 m terrain CSV.

score_definition.feature_score: 100 * (1 - |2F - 1|) where F is the percentile of the Earth cell value under the reference model built from the summary JSON (lognormal or Beta[min,max]; Gaussian only if forced). For z-score models this equals 100 * erfc(|z| / sqrt(2)).
score_definition.overall_score: sum_i(w_i * s_i) / sum_i(w_i) over available features; weights renormalised per cell.
score_definition.contribution: c_i = (w_i / W_available) * s_i; contributions sum to score (to rounding).
score_definition.omitted_per_cell: z-scores and x/y are not stored per cell to keep the file small; z-scores are in top_candidates.json for candidates, and x/y are in the input CSV (same row order as this file).
score_definition.null_meaning: score is null where fewer than minFeatures features or less than minWeightCompleteness of the weight were available.
score_definition.rank: 1 = highest overall score among scored cells at this scale; null if not scored.
score_definition.scale_properties: score_360m is the overall score of the 360 m parent cell against the 360 m reference; delta_360m = score - score_360m.

source.dataset: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m, Mar 2014 (USGS Astrogeology)
